Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- 50-year-old man presents with 4–5 days of feeling unwell: cough (mainly dry, some phlegm), runny nose, sore throat, mild ear symptoms, intermittent fevers/chills/sweating, shortness of breath, initial resolved diarrhea, and mild generalized myalgia/stiffness.
- Comorbidities include type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and overweight/obesity.
- Environmental/social factors: alcohol use (~9 pints/week), previously smoked (cutting down with vaporizer), lives with wife, works in manual role.
- No chest pain, no significant GI ongoing symptoms, appetite maintained.
- No physical examination or measured vital signs.
- DDx supports primary consideration of viral upper respiratory tract infection (URTI, including influenza), with possible but less likely bacterial lower respiratory tract infection (community-acquired pneumonia/bronchitis) or COVID-19.
- Plan discussed: conservative approach; symptomatic support (rest, fluids, paracetamol); delayed antibiotic prescription (Amoxicillin, one tablet three times daily, dose/route/frequency not documented) if no improvement in 24–48 hours; return for review if symptoms persist.

Management Plan
- Rest; maintain hydration; supportive care with paracetamol for fever/myalgia.
- Provided delayed script for antibiotics (Amoxicillin) to be used if symptoms do not improve in 24–48 hours (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Advised to return if symptoms persist beyond next week or worsen.
- Continue efforts to reduce smoking and alcohol as previously advised.
- No specific investigation or referrals documented.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
- Viral upper respiratory tract infection (including influenza or common cold): High likelihood. Fits acute onset with coryza, cough, sore throat, myalgia, mild systemic symptoms; expected clinical course.
- Bacterial lower respiratory infection (community-acquired pneumonia/bronchitis): Moderate likelihood. Raised due to comorbidities and SOB, but lacking focal severe features; current plan is to treat if unimproved.
- COVID-19: Moderate likelihood. Symptoms compatible, but no clear contact/exposure or mention of loss of smell/taste.
